subject: Clarify audit exposure across hosting modes (SOC 2 Type II) — NorthStar request
messages:
From: Tia Nguyen <tia.nguyen@northstarbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@finedge.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — please confirm which hosting modes are in-scope for NorthStar

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on — we are finalizing the SOC 2 Type II evidence request for NorthStar Bank and need to pin the hosting modalities that will be treated as "in-scope" for the audit period (2026-06-01 through 2027-05-31). Specifically, please confirm the following for the Redwood services NorthStar uses: hosted API (public), Dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity), and Private/VPC deployments (customer-managed connectors).

Questions: 
- For Dedicated pools that NorthStar has reserved, are they logically or physically isolated from other tenants, or does routing/fallback to a hosted tier occur under capacity pressure?
- If fallback/routing occurs, is that automatic at the request level, and is it within the audit period? If so, we need a bridge letter or an attestation describing when/why fallback was used.
- For Private/VPC installs used by NorthStar, confirm whether the control plane or any telemetry flows through Redwood-hosted infrastructure during normal operation.

Requested artifacts (if available):
- A short bridge letter template that would allow us to document any short-lived exceptions (e.g., fallback to hosted during a maintenance window)
- Deployment mapping (tenant-to-pool) for the period above (spreadsheet OK)
- A high-level diagram showing where logs/telemetry for Private/VPC customers traverse (if they leave the customer VPC)

If you prefer, we can take a call early next week — Evan (cc'd) is our audit lead and can coordinate. Appreciate a reply by end of week to avoid delaying our auditor schedule.

Best,
Tia Nguyen
Sr. InfoSec Manager, NorthStar Bank

---
Note: We are also running a short SIG/CAIQ mapping in parallel; if you have a pre-filled CAIQ for these hosting modes it would be helpful but isn’t required at this point.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tia Nguyen <tia.nguyen@northstarbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — please confirm which hosting modes are in-scope for NorthStar

Hi Tia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Legal / Compliance) and Marissa (Security Partnerships) so they can weigh in and help assemble the artifacts. Preliminary answers below; we’ll follow up with the requested attachments.

Quick summary: 
- Dedicated pools purchased under NorthStar’s commitment are tenant-isolated by default (logical isolation + dedicated GPU nodes). There are two exceptions where short-run routing to compatible hosted variants can happen: 1) scheduled maintenance window where Dedicated capacity is drained and 2) emergency failover in a severe hardware outage. Both are rare and governed by our incident runbooks.
- When fallback occurs it is policy-driven and requires a routing decision; it is not an automatic silent spillover — we track and log these events. For audit purposes we can provide a bridge letter that documents our fallback policy, examples of events in the audit period (if any), and an attestation about tenant isolation for active Dedicated reservations.
- Private/VPC deployments for NorthStar are configured with a customer-managed network path. The control plane remains logically separated; telemetry related to orchestration may traverse a Redwood egress path for optional observability features, but logs with customer data do not leave the customer VPC unless explicitly enabled by the customer. We will annotate the diagram to make this explicit.

Action items I will take this week:
1) Attach a bridge letter draft tailored to cover Dedicated->Hosted fallback events and an explanatory paragraph about maintenance windows.
2) Share a deployment mapping spreadsheet that ties NorthStar tenant IDs to pool names during the audit period.
3) Provide a network/telemetry diagram with callouts for any control-plane flows.

Kimberly / Marissa — want to add anything on the legal/attestation side before I send the draft to Tia?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
From: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@finedge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tia Nguyen <tia.nguyen@northstarbank.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — please confirm which hosting modes are in-scope for NorthStar

Karthik / Tia — quick clarifications from the audit team so we can scope evidence collection: 

1) If Dedicated -> Hosted routing occurred even once in the audit period, we will need an entry in the bridge letter describing the event(s) and the mitigation steps. A date range + short narrative is sufficient.
2) For Private/VPC, the auditor will want a statement on whether any customer PII or auth tokens left the customer-managed network during the audit period. If observability was enabled and sent to Redwood telemetry endpoints, we will need to know which signals (metric names, log categories) and whether PII was filtered before egress.

We have a tight window; if you can provide the draft bridge letter and mapping by EOD today we will slot it into the evidence binder. If not, a DocuSign-enabled bridge letter we can sign while final items come in will work.

Thanks — Evan
Lead Auditor, FineEdge Compliance Services

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — please confirm which hosting modes are in-scope for NorthStar

Tia / Evan — attaching the requested artifacts and next steps.

Attachments: northstar_bridge_letter_dedicated_vpc.pdf, deployment_mapping_northstar.xlsx

Key points captured in the bridge letter (attached):
- Dedicated pools for NorthStar are tenant-isolated during normal operations.
- We document two conditions where routing to Redwood-hosted variants can occur: scheduled maintenance (planned window) and emergency hardware failover. The letter includes a short narrative template for any specific events during the audit period; if you provide event dates we will append them to the attestation.
- For Private/VPC, the control plane does perform orchestration calls to customer-managed endpoints but customer data is not forwarded to Redwood telemetry by default. If NorthStar enabled additional observability in the period under review, we’ve noted which signal categories may have egressed and confirmed PII filtering rules.

DocuSign for bridge letter: https://app.docusign.com/Na7/sign/ABCD1234-bridge-letter
Evidence folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-northstar-audit-evidence

Next steps: 
- If you want the signed bridge letter in the binder today, use the DocuSign link and we’ll countersign.
- If you prefer an amended attestation referencing specific fallback events, share the dates and rough narrative and we will update the attached PDF.

Kimberly and Marissa are on standby for any clarifying language.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
